name: Logan International Airport
text: Boston's airport on landfill in the harbour, a short cab ride through the Callahan Tunnel from downtown. Eastern's shuttle leaves for New York and Washington every hour on the hour, no reservation needed.

name: John F. Kennedy International Airport
text: The gateway to the world on Jamaica Bay, each airline with its own terminal around the central loop, from TWA's winged Flight Center to Pan Am's flying saucer Worldport. The Concorde leaves for London and Paris every day.

name: LaGuardia Airport
text: New York's crowded airport on Flushing Bay, closest to Manhattan, for flights inside the country. The Eastern Air-Shuttle and the Pan Am Shuttle run hourly to Boston and Washington from their own terminals.

name: Newark International Airport
text: The airport in the Jersey Meadows, where People Express sells cheap seats and collects the fares on board after takeoff. Two modern terminals stand beside the New Jersey Turnpike, a third still unfinished.

name: Washington National Airport
text: Congress's own airport on the Potomac, a Metro stop from the Capitol, its perimeter rule keeping jets to shorter flights. Planes follow the river to land, the monuments off the left wing.

name: Washington Dulles International Airport
text: Eero Saarinen's swooping terminal far out in the Virginia countryside, its wings lifted on leaning pillars. Mobile lounges on stilts carry passengers out to the planes.

name: Baltimore-Washington International Airport
text: The renamed Friendship Airport between Baltimore and Washington, Piedmont Airlines' busy hub. An Amtrak station on the Northeast Corridor opened beside it in 1980.

name: O'Hare International Airport
text: The world's busiest airport, where United and American trade connecting passengers by the thousand every hour. The rapid transit has reached the terminal since 1984, forty minutes from the Loop.

name: Chicago Midway Airport
text: The old municipal airport, a square mile boxed in by Southwest Side bungalows, once the busiest in the world. Midway Airlines brought jets back here in 1979.

name: Philadelphia International Airport
text: Philadelphia's airport on the Delaware riverbank in the southwest of the city. The airport rail line from Center City opened in 1985.

name: Hartsfield Atlanta International Airport
text: The midfield terminal of 1980, the biggest in the world, with an underground people mover linking its long parallel concourses. Delta and Eastern hub here, and they say you change planes in Atlanta even on the way to heaven.

terminals.name: Maynard H. Jackson Junior International Terminal

name: Miami International Airport
text: Eastern's southern hub and Pan Am's gateway to Latin America, its long finger concourses busy with flights to the Caribbean. Cargo jets for South America crowd the north side.

name: Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport
text: Broward County's airport beside Port Everglades, for snowbirds and spring breakers. Thirty miles north of Miami, it is often the cheaper fare.

name: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport
text: Detroit's main airport in Romulus, twenty miles west of downtown, the hub of Republic Airlines until Northwest bought it this year. Its Smith and Davey terminals date from the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Detroit City Airport
text: The small city airport on the East Side off Gratiot Avenue, five miles from downtown. Commuter flights and private planes use it now that the airlines have moved to Metro.

name: Lambert-St. Louis International Airport
text: TWA's hub under the vaulted concrete domes of Minoru Yamasaki's 1956 terminal. TWA took over Ozark Air Lines this year and now runs most of the flights.

name: McCarran International Airport
text: The airport at the south end of the Strip, slot machines waiting at the gates for arriving gamblers. Junket charters and jets from every western city fill the ramp on weekends.

name: Robert Mueller Municipal Airport
text: Austin's small airport three miles northeast of the Capitol, its one terminal on Airport Boulevard. Jets climb out low over the neighbourhoods around it.

name: Los Angeles International Airport
text: The horseshoe of terminals around the Theme Building's flying-saucer arches, rebuilt for the 1984 Olympics with an upper deck and the new Tom Bradley International Terminal. Jets roar in over Inglewood day and night.

name: Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport
text: The old Lockheed Air Terminal in the San Fernando Valley, where you walk across the tarmac and climb the stairs to the plane. PSA flies from here to San Francisco for less than a tank of gas.

name: Long Beach Airport
text: Long Beach's Streamline Moderne terminal of 1941, beside the Douglas plant where DC-9s and MD-80s are built. Jet America and a few others fly from here, under strict noise rules.

name: San Francisco International Airport
text: United's Pacific gateway on the bay shore south of the city, its horseshoe of terminals around a central garage. Fog often slows the landings to one runway in the summer.

name: Oakland International Airport
text: The East Bay's airport on bay fill near the Coliseum, a BART shuttle bus ride from the Coliseum station. Less crowded and less foggy than SFO.

name: San Jose International Airport
text: Silicon Valley's airport, two miles from downtown San Jose, busy with engineers flying out for the week. Its small terminals keep the curb a short walk from the gate.
